title: Incident stakeholder messaging quickref
body:
Purpose and scope:
This quickref is a compact runbook for incident-facing communications: what to say on the status page, how to message customers and partners, and a short internal war-room checklist to keep updates concise and consistent. It is intentionally lightweight for rapid adoption during incidents (SEV1-SEV3).

When to use this document:
- Use when the incident requires external signaling (customer-facing outage, partial degradation, throttling events).
- Use for targeted customer outreach when there are clear impact buckets (data loss, latency above SLO, unavailable API endpoints).
- Use as the single source of truth for message cadence until post-incident comms are finalized.

Audience segmentation (who gets what):
- All customers (broadcast status page) — for platform-wide degradations or outages.
- Affected customers (targeted email/slack) — for tenant-specific incidents, data/PII concerns, or contractual SLAs.
- Internal engineering & SRE (war-room updates) — technical detail, mitigation steps, runbook actions.
- Executives & sales/customer success — short impact summary, customer list, mitigations and timelines.

Roles and responsibilities (quick):
- Bridge lead: owns update cadence, assigns tasks, validates external messaging.
- Comms lead: drafts status page and customer copy; coordinates with legal/PR for sensitive incidents.
- Engineering lead: provides technical status, root cause hypotheses, and ETA for next milestone.
- CS/AM liaison: identifies high-risk customers to notify and provides contact details.
- Scribe: records timeline, decisions, and all status updates (confluence/Jira).

War-room checklist (first 20 minutes):
1) Confirm scope: affected services, regions, customers.
2) Set incident severity level and create ticket (include tags: component, region, severity).
3) Bridge lead sets cadence: initial +15m, +30m, +60m then hourly (adjust if resolution faster).
4) Publish initial status page entry (short, factual). Use template A (below).
5) CS/AM liaison triages customer list; decide targeted notifications.
6) Assign immediate mitigation work (workstreams: rollback, capacity, routing/fallback).
7) Start a running timeline (scribe).
8) If customer data may be affected, notify security & legal immediately.

Update cadence guidance:
- Initial: within 15 minutes of detection (even if only acknowledgment).
- Substantial progress: whenever there is a material change (new ETA, mitigation succeeded/failed).
- Regular cadence: until resolved, update at least every 30–60 minutes for SEV1; SEV2 every 60–120 minutes.
- Resolution notice: once fully restored, publish final status and plan for postmortem.

Public status page templates
(keep short + explicit; use plain language; include impact, scope, ETA if available):
Template A — Initial acknowledgement (short)
Title: "Investigating degraded performance for API/text-generation"
Body: "We are currently investigating increased latency affecting text generation APIs. Some requests are delayed or time out. Engineers are actively investigating. We will provide updates within 30 minutes. Affected regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1. Status: Investigating."

Template B — Ongoing update (progress)
Title: "Mitigation in progress — reduced error rate for text generation"
Body: "We deployed a routing change that has reduced errors by ~40% for most customers. A subset of requests remain impacted. Engineers are continuing to roll out additional mitigations; we expect another update in ~45 minutes. Impact: intermittent errors and elevated latency. Status: Partial mitigation in progress."

Template C — Resolution
Title: "Resolved — text generation API restored"
Body: "All services have been restored and normal request rates are observed. If you continue to see any issues, please contact support@redwood.ai with request ID and timestamps. Root cause analysis is pending. Status: Resolved."

Template D — Root cause known (post-resolution brief)
Title: "Root cause identified — overloaded autoscaler logic"
Body: "We identified that a misconfiguration in the autoscaler caused excessive scaling churn during a traffic spike, which led to elevated latencies and transient errors. Fix: reverted autoscaler config and improved cooldown settings. We're scheduling a postmortem and will share a timeline for mitigations in 5 business days. Status: Root cause identified; mitigation applied."

Targeted customer communication examples
(keep subject lines explicit; first paragraph = impact summary; second = mitigation/what we did; third = next steps + contacts)
Severity: Critical (tenant data unavailability)
Subject: "[Action required] Temporary data unavailability for Redwood workspace: <workspace-name>"
Body: "Hi <Customer-Name>,

We experienced temporary unavailability for <workspace-name> between 2025-02-14T10:02Z and 2025-02-14T10:48Z. During this window, API reads returned 503 errors for cached model outputs; stored assets were not deleted. Engineers implemented a targeted routing rollback at 10:38Z that restored access.

What you need to know: No user data was deleted. If you see failures when fetching recent outputs, please retry requests; persistent issues should be reported to your CS lead. We will follow up with a full timeline and RCA within 5 business days.

Contacts: <CS-rep> (cs@example.com) and incident-ops@redwood.ai

Apologies for the disruption; we’re committed to preventing recurrence."

Severity: Partial degradation (affects latency-sensitive customers)
Subject: "Latency impact on embedding generation — targeted notice for heavy-utilization customers"
Body: "Hi <Customer-Name>,

You may experience elevated latency for embedding requests (median latency up from 120ms to ~450ms) between 2025-02-14T09:30Z and ongoing. We’ve applied a priority routing policy for customers on dedicated plans which reduced impact for most tenants.

If you are on a dedicated cluster or have specific SLO needs, your CS/AM has been notified and can enable a temporary bypass or increase capacity. If you'd like us to take action, reply to this email with the workspace id.

We’ll share a follow-up when the incident is fully resolved."

Executive internal brief (one-line + one paragraph)
Subject: "Incident brief — text-gen latency, partial regional impact"
Body: "Summary: Increased latency in text-generation (us-west-2, eu-west-1) affecting ~12% of requests; no customer data loss. Mitigation: routing update and temporary capacity bump applied; observed ~70% reduction in errors. Next: roll out autoscaler fix and schedule RCA.

ETA for resolution: 2–4 hours; RCA within 5 business days. Impacted customers: list in Jira RED-1234."

Guidance: tone, legal, and billing
- Tone: Be factual, avoid speculation, don’t assign blame in public messages. Use plain language.
- Legal/PR: route any messages that mention customer data, regulatory impact, or security incidents to Legal and Security before broad distribution.
- Billing: do not promise credits; route requests to Billing/Finance for approval. Use neutral language: "We will review eligibility for service credits after the RCA."

Post-incident follow-ups and postmortem messaging
- Final status page entry should include a short summary, timeline highlights, and high-level next steps.
- Postmortem public note (if applicable) should be cleared with Engineering + Legal + Product and be published within 5 business days for SEV1 incidents.
- Customer-facing RCA should include: what happened, scope, impact, short-term mitigations, long-term fixes, and timeline for when fixes will be implemented.

Checklist for finalizing communications (closure tasks):
- Confirm all affected customers have been notified where required.
- Publish final status and mark incident status = Resolved.
- Open RCA/retro ticket and assign owners for long-term fixes.
- Notify Sales/CS of any customers needing follow-up.
- Tag incident tickets with communication artifacts (status page entries, customer emails).

Quick snippets and placeholders (copy-paste friendly)
- Placeholder for ETA: "We expect to have a mitigation in place within approximately <ETA>. We will update sooner if we have new information."
- Placeholder for affected customers: "Affected: customers using <feature> in <region>. We are contacting customers on paid plans directly."
- Closure sentence: "We will follow up with a detailed root cause analysis and timeline for preventative measures."

Tips and common pitfalls
- Don’t wait for a root cause to post the initial status page — post an acknowledgment.
- Avoid technical jargon in public messages; keep the internal war-room highly technical.
- Avoid multiple simultaneous channels for the same audience (e.g., don’t send duplicate public tweets + status page entries with diverging messages).
- For multi-tenant incidents, prefer targeted emails for customers with contractual SLAs.

Appendix: sample emergency timeline format (for scribe)
- 10:02Z — Alert triggered: elevated 5xxs on text-gen-prod.
- 10:05Z — Bridge opened; initial status posted (Template A).
- 10:12Z — Routing change implemented (partial improvement).
- 10:38Z — Targeted rollback completed; latency trending to normal.
- 10:48Z — Monitoring confirms recovery; final status posted (Template C).

Notes and next steps for this runbook copy:
- This file should serve as an on-call quickref — keep concise and actionable.
- Add region-specific contact lists and CS owner mapping in the linked Confluence page.
- Consider creating a short Slack snippet set for easier copy-paste during incidents.

End of quickref.

Document history:
- Drafted by Maya Chen on 2024-10-28.
- Inputs from Oliver Singh and Priya Nair (CS procedures) added 2024-11-15.
